append.text: **Ps 36:14b *páuperem et ínopem* → *o pobre e o indigente*: unknown to the blind reader for the FOURTH time in four readings (Pss 11 ×2, 13, 36).** Kept on the row so the evidence stays in one place. **Proposal for a ruling: *inops* → *desvalido* psalter-wide** (MS1932 in Ps 11; keeps *pobre* for pauper and the pair's two words).

**Ps 36:17 *confírmat autem justos Dóminus* → draft 2 *mas o Senhor sustenta os justos*:** draft 1 *confirma os justos* was heard by the blind reader as 'reconhece ou atesta que eles são justos'. With persons as object *confirmar* is heard as attesting; *sustentar* (ὑποστηρίζει, 'props up'; free — sustinére is *esperar por*, D36) passed the Latinist. The Tuesday Matins antiphon *Brácchia peccatórum * conteréntur, confírmat autem justos Dóminus* follows. Proposal: *confirmar* only where a thing or a word is confirmed; with persons, *sustentar* (or *firmar*).

Ps 36:11 *in multitúdine pacis* → *na multidão da paz*: the stylist asked *numa multidão de paz* (heard as a crowd); the blind reader heard 'abundância de paz' first, a crowd second. Kept; passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 36:20 *deficiéntes, quemádmodum fumus defícient* → *desfalecendo, desfalecerão como a fumaça*** (draft 2; the two forms together, as the participle + verb row, the stylist's order). The blind reader heard vanishing like smoke and listed *desfalecendo / desfalecerão* as unknown; the Latinist (minor, draft 2) asked *desvanecendo-se, desvanecer-se-ão* — refused for the row. 101:4 *defecérunt sicut fumus dies mei* should agree.

**Ps 36:40 *et liberábit eos: et éruet eos a peccatóribus* → *e os livrará: * e os arrancará dos pecadores*** — the row's case (side by side with liberáre, with a source). Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked.

**Ps 36:37–38 *sunt relíquiæ hómini pacífico … relíquiæ impiórum interíbunt* → *há um resto para o homem de paz … o resto dos ímpios se extinguirá*** (one decision `reliquiae`, singular *resto* both times; a third Greek word, ἐγκατάλειμμα). The blind reader heard 'something is left, unclear what' (37) and 'the wicked still alive' (38); passed the Latinist twice. Options *restos*, *descendência*.

**Ps 36:31 *non supplantabúntur gressus ejus* → *e os seus passos não serão derrubados*:** draft 3 had the row's option for gressus, *não tropeçarão* (intransitive) — the Latinist marked it MAJOR (the passive lost). *fazer tropeçar* has no passive, so with gressus as subject the row's *derrubar* serves; passed the gate. Commune C5 versicle *Lex Dei ejus in corde ipsíus: et non supplantabúntur gressus ejus* follows. 139:5 *supplantáre gressus meos* (active, object) can still take *fazer tropeçar*.
Ps 36:25, 26, 28b → *descendência* ×3 (*nem a sua descendência buscando pão*; *e a sua descendência será abençoada*; *e a descendência dos ímpios perecerá*). No plant image; no reader remarked.

Ps 36:23 *Apud Dóminum gressus hóminis dirigéntur* → *Junto do Senhor serão dirigidos os passos do homem* (MS1932 *pelo Senhor* the option). The blind reader heard 'o Senhor orientará' (and, second, 'when near the Lord'); passed the Latinist twice.
Ps 36:37 *vide æquitátem* → *vê a equidade*: unknown to the blind reader again (the antiphon *Custódi innocéntiam * et vide æquitátem*); kept.

Ps 36:9 *exterminabúntur* (exterminári, ἐξολεθρευθήσονται) → *serão exterminados* — the cognate, shared with dispérdere: the two never meet in a verse (exterminári only 36:9, 79:14, grep). Ps 36 keeps the Latin's other verbs of ending apart: períre → perecer, disperíre → *perecer de todo* (36:22, 38; 82:11 to follow), interíre → *extinguir-se* (36:38; 48:18 of a man will want *morrer*).
Ps 36:27a *Declína a malo, et fac bonum* → *Aparta-te do mal, e faz o bem* (= 33:15a, the formula row); passed the Latinist twice.

Ps 36:32 *Consíderat peccátor justum* → *O pecador observa o justo* (a person, 21:18's build), kept apart from 36:12 *Observábit peccátor justum* → *O pecador espreitará o justo* (observáre, παρατηρήσεται).

Ps 36:23 *et viam ejus volet* → *e ele quererá o seu caminho*: the blind reader heard the man wanting the Lord's way — the Latin leaves subject and owner open; DRB *he shall like well his way* (*se agradará do seu caminho*) the option.

Ps 36:3 *fac bonitátem* (no person) → *usa de bondade*, kept apart from 36:27 *fac bonum* → *faz o bem* (= 33:15a). The stylist found it ceremonious and asked *faz o bem* — refused for that collision; passed the Latinist twice.
Ps 36:13 *quóniam próspicit quod véniet dies ejus* → *porque prevê que virá o seu dia* (προβλέπει, the row's 'sees ahead' sense); passed the Latinist twice, heard rightly (the Lord foresees).
Ps 36:6 *Et edúcet quasi lumen justítiam tuam* → *E fará sair a tua justiça como a luz*; the stylist asked *fará surgir* (breath) — refused for the row.
Ps 36:13 *Dóminus autem irridébit eum* → *Mas o Senhor rirá dele*.
Ps 36:9 *sustinéntes autem Dóminum, ipsi hereditábunt terram* → *mas os que esperam pelo Senhor, esses herdarão a terra* (D36); 36:34 *Exspécta Dóminum* → *Aguarda o Senhor* (= 26:14).

Ps 36:11 *Mansuéti autem hereditábunt terram* → *Mas os mansos herdarão a terra*. Mt 5:4 in the Clementine (fetched, consult/bolls-VULG-40-5.json) has another Latin, *Beati mites: quoniam ipsi possidebunt terram*; the Greek (Tischendorf, consult/bolls-TISCH-40-5.json) is the LXX's κληρονομήσουσιν τὴν γῆν. The psalm keeps its own verb, *herdar*.
Ps 36:26 *Tota die miserétur et cómmodat* → *O dia todo tem piedade e empresta* — applied.

Ps 36:27, 36:29 → *pelos séculos dos séculos*: the Latinist asked the singular (minor) at both, twice (drafts 3 and 4); the stylist asked to move the formula off the final (proparoxytone). Both refused under D27.
Ps 36:38 *Injústi autem disperíbunt simul* → *Mas os injustos juntos perecerão de todo* (the stylist's order, *juntos* next to the verb).
**Ps 36:27a copies it:** *Aparta-te do mal, e faz o bem: * e habita pelos séculos dos séculos*.

terms: | æmulári | ter inveja de (*Não tenhas inveja dos malvados*) | open | Ps 36:1, 36:7, 36:8 (παραζηλόω ×3; one phrase three times; 36:8 without an object: *não tenhas inveja, a ponto de fazeres o mal*). L&S's bad sense 'be envious of'. The Hebrew's 'fret not' is not the Latin's. Only here (77:58 has the noun *æmulatiónem*, grep). The Tuesday Matins antiphon *Noli æmulári * in eo qui prosperátur et facit iniquitátem* follows. Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked. Options *invejar* (MS1932), *rivalizar com*. |

| zeláre | invejar (*nem invejes os que fazem a iniquidade*) | open | Ps 36:1, beside *æmulári* (the Greek's simple ζήλου beside its compound παραζήλου: one root, so the verb of *inveja*). 72:3 *Quia zelávi super iníquos* should follow (*invejei*). *ter ciúme de* (the cognate) is a lover's jealousy in Brazil; *ter zelo por* the opposite sense. zelus (noun) keeps *zelo* (118:139). |

| malignári (the verb) | fazer o mal (*a ponto de fazeres o mal … os que fazem o mal*) | open | Ps 36:8–9 (πονηρεύομαι); the participle as a noun stays *malvados* (D24, 36:1). 104:15 *nolíte malignári* (grep) should take *não façais o mal*. |

| fácere iniquitátem / injustítias | fazer a iniquidade / fazer injustiças | open | Ps 36:1, 36:7 (ποιέω); *praticar* stays operári's (5:7a, 6:9). The stylist asked *praticam* at 36:1 — refused for that reason. |
| ólera herbárum | as ervas verdes | open | Ps 36:2 only (λάχανα χλόης; DRB *the green herbs*). |

| páscere (passive) | ser apascentado (*e serás apascentado nas suas riquezas*) | open | Ps 36:3 (ποιμανθήσῃ). **Unknown to the blind reader**; kept for the shepherd's image. *ser alimentado* (DRB *fed*) the option. Other places not yet counted (grep before use). |

| reveláre (a way, to someone) | revelar (*Revela ao Senhor o teu caminho*) | open | Ps 36:5 (ἀποκάλυψον; not the Hebrew's 'commit'); the monastic antiphon *Revéla * Dómino viam meam* and the Alleluia of 01-31 (grep). The glossary's other reveláre builds (118:18 *desvendar* the eyes, 28:9 *desnudar* the woods) stand; options *Descobre*, *Expõe* (MS1932). Passed the Latinist twice. |

| súbditus esse | ser sujeito a (*sê sujeito ao Senhor*) | open | Ps 36:6 (ὑποτάγηθι); the family of *sujeitar* (subdere / subjícere, 17:48). The stylist asked *sê submisso* — option; the blind reader did not stumble. |

| observáre (a person, with hostile intent) | espreitar (*O pecador espreitará o justo*) | open | Ps 36:12 (παρατηρήσεται), kept apart from 36:32 *consíderat* → *observa*. **Unknown to the blind reader**; passed the Latinist twice. *observar* (serváre, 30:7) the option. |
| deícere | abater (*Para abater o pobre e o indigente*) | open | Ps 36:14b (καταβαλεῖν); *derrubar* is supplantáre's (17:40, 36:31). |
| trucidáre | massacrar (*para massacrar os retos de coração*) | open | Ps 36:14b only (σφάξαι); draft 1 *trucidar* was unknown to the blind reader. |

| mutuári / commodáre | tomar emprestado / emprestar | open | Ps 36:21 *Mutuábitur peccátor* → *O pecador tomará emprestado*; 36:26 *miserétur et cómmodat* → *tem piedade e empresta* (one Greek verb in two voices, δανείζομαι / δανείζω; the Latin two verbs). 111:5 *qui miserétur et cómmodat* should copy 36:26. |

| disperíre / interíre | perecer de todo / extinguir-se | open | Ps 36:22, 36:38 (ἐξολεθρεύω behind both); disperíre also 82:11, interíre 48:18 (of a man: *morrer* there). The Latin's five verbs of ending in Ps 36 kept apart (see *dispérdere*). |
| collídere (passive) | ser esmagado (*Quando cair, não será esmagado*) | open | Ps 36:24 only (καταραχθήσεται); *quebrar* is confríngere's. |

| mortificáre | dar a morte (*e busca dar-lhe a morte*) | open | Ps 36:32 (θανατῶσαι); 43:22 *mortificámur tota die*, 78:11, 108:17 (grep). The cognate *mortificar* is ascetic self-denial to a Catholic ear. |
| superexaltáre | muito exaltar (*Vi o ímpio muito exaltado*) | open | Ps 36:35 only; draft 3 *sumamente exaltado* (MS1932) was bookish to the stylist and unknown to the blind reader. |

| pacíficus (of a man) | de paz (*para o homem de paz*) | open | Ps 36:37 (εἰρηνικῷ); the cognate *pacífico* is proparoxytone at the final (the stylist). 119:7 *eram pacíficus* (grep) will decide its own build. |
